title: Cycle lifts and finite ideal-multiple differentials in a quotient tensor complex
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, I an ideal of R, M an R-module, and P→M a projective resolution (projective terms [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] and exact augmented complex [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]). Form C=P⊗_R R/I, with cycles and their inclusion as in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Every z∈Z_1(C) admits y∈P_1, a natural number k, a:Fin(k)→I, and p:Fin(k)→P_0 such that iCycles(z)=y⊗1 and d_P y=Σ_j a_j p_j. No freeness hypothesis on the terms of P is necessary.

source.place: Parent lem-weil-pbc-tor-ideal-comparison-compatibility, Step 2; Algebra, Section 00LY, proof of 00M5 and Remark 00M6. The quotient-complex details are expanded explicitly here.

proof.text: Let e:P_1⊗R/I≃P_1/(I•P_1) be TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul. Lift e(iCycles(z)) through the surjective quotient map to y. The formula tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul_tmul_mk for y⊗mk_I(1) proves iCycles(z)=y⊗1.

Apply iCycles_d to z and substitute the lift. The mapped differential on a pure tensor is (d_P y)⊗1, so this tensor is zero. Apply tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul in degree zero and Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero to conclude d_P y∈I•P_0.

Induct on this membership with Submodule.smul_induction_on. A single product a•p is a sum indexed by Fin(1). For a sum of expressions indexed by Fin(k₁) and Fin(k₂), concatenate both coefficient and vector families with Fin.addCases and use Fin.sum_univ_add. This gives the required finite expression and completes the claimed witnesses.

theorem exists_quotient_cycle_lift
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (P : ProjectiveResolution M)
    (z : ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj
        (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).cycles 1) :
    ∃ (y : P.complex.X 1) (k : ℕ) (a : Fin k → I) (p : Fin k → P.complex.X 0),
      ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj
        (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj P.complex).iCycles 1 z = y ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : R ⧸ I) ∧
      P.complex.d 1 0 y = ∑ j, (a j : R) • p j
